findings.candidate: Crafted config.json redirects a preset's API key to an attacker URL (key exfiltration)
findings.disproof: Registry-wins is enforced at every read/write path: providers.normalize_config M7 overwrites provider_base_url with the registry endpoint for any known preset at config LOAD (auditor attack sim: {'provider':'xiaomi-mimo','provider_base_url':'https://evil.example/v1'} -> https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1); providers.save_payload re-resolves at save; settings_view.start_fetch queries the registry URL, never widget contents. The stored URL for presets is dead data.

findings.candidate: Malformed provider/variant values crash or bypass the recording guard / dialect selection
findings.disproof: All resolvers are isinstance-guarded and fail safe (resolve_provider_id(42)->'custom'; dialect_for_preset('junk')->'openai'; save_payload accepts labels/ids/None without raising — fuzz-verified). Non-str config values (e.g. JSON null model) pass through M4 byte-identical and can raise AttributeError on .strip() in main.start_recording (main.py:229-232) — PRE-EXISTING pattern (the baseline guard had identical .strip() semantics), same-user config tampering only, fail-closed (no request issued, no key material in the traceback: 'NoneType object has no attribute strip'). Recorded as HN-11, non-blocking.

findings.candidate: MiMo payload builder can be tricked into logging transcript/prompt content
findings.disproof: llm_payloads.py contains zero logging/print calls and imports nothing (AST-verified). llm_api logs exactly one line per request: description + _safe_url_for_log URL (llm_api.py:166). Stage-1 payloads contain no transcript in either dialect; the stage-2 prompt (with raw transcript) never reaches a log sink. Arabic prompts are module literals, never logged. Full logger call-site inventory across all 6 changed modules: zero transcript/prompt/key interpolation.

findings.candidate: HN-9 retained: _endpoint invalid-scheme error echoes base_url!r before the credential check
findings.detail: llm_api.py:108-111 raises with f'Provider Base URL is invalid: {base_url!r}' BEFORE the userinfo/query/fragment rejection at :114-118, so a typo'd-scheme URL containing user:pass@ echoes the credential into the UI-facing error message. Impact bounded: LLMError messages reach only the user's own UI (display-only, never logged). Suggested fix unchanged: run the credential rejection first or redact userinfo in the message.

findings.candidate: Module-size headroom: providers.py and llm_api.py sit at 349/350 lines
findings.detail: Within the gate (<=350) but with zero headroom. Both modules are cohesive (registry / transport); further growth should extract, not extend.

findings.candidate: Custom-URL mode sends the configured API key to whatever URL the config names
findings.detail: By design: Custom (OpenAI-compatible URL) makes the user the URL authority (README documents 'any URL you enter'). A same-user attacker who can write config.json could point Custom at an attacker host and harvest the key — but that attacker can already replace the binary; cross-user tampering is blocked by per-user config location (%LOCALAPPDATA%/WhisperLive, exact ACL fact already carried as needs_validation in SEC-D2-01 for Linux). Mitigations present: the 8 presets are immune (registry-wins, SEC-F-01); _endpoint still forbids credential-bearing URLs and logs are redacted. Accepted and documented.
